references.text: Jesus' mother had just said to the servants: "Whatever he tells you, do it" ([ref:Joh 2:5|John 2:5]). The servants' obedience in verse 8 – that they drew water and carried it to the master of the banquet – is a direct fulfillment of this instruction.

In [ref:Joh 2:7|John 2:7] Jesus told the servants to fill the jars with water. Verse 8 is the natural continuation where Jesus gives the next instruction, and the servants continue to obey without hesitation.

In [ref:Joh 2:9-10|John 2:9-10] the master of the banquet discovers that the water has become wine. Jesus' command in verse 8 to carry it to the master of the banquet sets the stage for this revelation of the miracle.

In [ref:Joh 4:46-50|John 4:46-50] we read about the royal official's faith in Cana, where the man "went" in obedience to Jesus' word. The pattern of obeying Jesus' command in faith – without seeing the result beforehand – is the same as that shown by the servants in John 2:8.

In [ref:Joh 9:7|John 9:7] Jesus commands the blind man to go and wash in the Pool of Siloam. The man obeys in faith without seeing the result beforehand, just as the servants in Cana carried the water to the master of the banquet without knowing it had become wine.

At Lazarus' tomb, Jesus tells them to roll away the stone ([ref:Joh 11:39-40|John 11:39-40]). As in the wedding miracle, people act in obedience to Jesus' word, and the result is that God's glory is revealed through a sign.

In [ref:2 Mos 7:19-20|Exodus 7:19-20] God turns the water in Egypt into blood through Moses. Jesus' turning of water into wine in Cana mirrors this as a positive counterpart – where God turned water into blood through judgment, Jesus graciously gives water as wine.

[ref:Joh 2:11|John 2:11] summarizes the entire event as "the beginning of Jesus' signs" where he revealed his glory. The servants' obedience in verse 8 was necessary for this sign to be performed and his glory to be revealed.

[ref:Jes 25:6|Isaiah 25:6] prophesies about a feast with good wine that the Lord will prepare for all peoples. Jesus' miracle in Cana, where he serves the best wine to the master of the banquet, is a foretaste of the abundance of this messianic feast.
